audit.whatIsWrong: Full-layer level chart reads 'Skill' on all seven rows while the content layer and the packet chart both read Ekko/Ekko/Skill/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko/Azir. The page renders two different answers to who wins each stage.
audit.why: Ekko's 1075-range Q out-ranges Azir's 740 Q and 525 soldier auto-range early, and Azir's only escape (Shifting Sands, 22s at rank 1) is a long cooldown; late, Emperor's Divide creates terrain that blocks Ekko's E dash and Azir out-ranges every string.
audit.corrected: Align full phases[].side/.rating/.why to the content win[] chart: Ekko rows 0,1,3,4,5; Skill row 2; Azir row 6.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text never names a real cooldown, and the level 6 line does not say what Chronobreak actually costs.
audit.why: Chronobreak is 110/80/50 and Shifting Sands is 22/20.5/19/17.5/16 — those numbers are what make 'commit now' concrete.
audit.corrected: Phases 4 and 5 rewritten with the 110s Chronobreak and the Shifting Sands window; cooldowns field now carries both.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive interactions are absent: Shifting Sands (E) shields Azir through the burst window, and Emperor's Divide (R) creates terrain that blocks Ekko's E dash.
audit.why: Both are in the kits (E flags shield+dash; R flag terrain 'creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes') and neither reaches the page. The missingInteractions entry flags the shield case explicitly.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, enemyWin, report[5].t and phases[6].why now state both.

audit.whatIsWrong: breakdown.cooldowns contained no digit at all (lint COOLDOWN_NO_DIGIT).
audit.why: It is the one field that must hold real cooldowns.
audit.corrected: Rewritten with 22s/16s Shifting Sands, 120s Emperor's Divide, 110s Chronobreak.

audit.whatIsWrong: dosFull[1].d was the tradeGood string verbatim and dontsFull[2].d was the tradeBad string verbatim, under unrelated titles (lint COPY_PASTE_BLEED x2).
audit.why: The title promises one thing and the body explains another.
audit.corrected: Both bodies rewritten to match their own titles, grounded in Ekko's 9s E and 110s R.

edits.before: Q the wave and his toes — the return pass chunks; learn the slow zone's drag on his dodge patterns.
edits.after: Q both passes through him — the return chunks, and a 525-range soldier cannot answer a 1075-range grenade.

edits.before: E blink-strike window opens: Q-E-auto is your first real trade and the third passive hit stings already.
edits.after: E opens the blink-strike: Q, E the gap, auto for the third passive hit — Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1.

edits.before: Three-hit trades on cooldown — Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk. Bank the tempo for 6.
edits.after: Q in, E the gap, passive proc, walk — his 19s E escapes one of these, not three. Bank tempo for 6.

edits.before: Chronobreak online — your aggression gets a save file. Trade like the rewind exists, because it does.
edits.after: Chronobreak at 110s underwrites the dive — commit through the soldiers and rewind out of whatever answers.

edits.before: First item spike: the full string deletes half bars and the rewind erases the counter-argument.
edits.after: First item: the full string deletes half his bar, and W's stun catches him the moment his E is spent.

edits.before: Late Ekko picks and survives: dive the carry, W the peel, and Chronobreak out of whatever they answered with.
edits.after: Emperor's Divide is terrain: it walls your E mid-dash and his soldiers out-range every string. Take picks, not fronts.

edits.before: - Azir Shifting Sands: matchup-defining — His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. Read it like a second minimap. - Guard your R Chronobreak like a fifth summoner spell. - Ultimate goes to kill windows only.
edits.after: - Shifting Sands is 22s at rank 1 and 16s at rank 5 — his shield and his only escape in one button, so commit the second it is gone. - Emperor's Divide is 120s and walls your E mid-dash. - Chronobreak is 110s early: spend it on kills.

edits.before: Azir wins by landing Shifting Sands, denying your pattern, and renting you the lane at a range markup.
edits.after: Azir wins by poking from soldier range, dashing off your engage, and walling your E out with Emperor's Divide.

edits.before: Carry through insured dives — one carry per rewind cycle; your job is spending R as a weapon, not an apology.
edits.after: Carry by killing him before the soldiers land — one escape on 16s, no peel once it is gone. That is your window.

edits.before: Q through him, E the gap, passive third hit, walk out through the slow — the full string chunks and the return pass pays the exit.
edits.after: Never open a string without E: it is the gap-closer and the exit both, and 9s at rank 1 is a long time in his soldier line.

edits.before: Blinking in with R down against a loaded kit — Ekko without the rewind is a mid laner doing parkour at a funeral.
edits.after: Chronobreak is 110s at rank 1 and 50s at rank 3 — a rewind held all game is a summoner spell you never cast.

edits.before: Track Azir’s Shifting Sands: His shield-dash to a soldier — engage the window after he burns it. The whole green-light system is its cooldown.
edits.after: Track Shifting Sands (22s at rank 1): it shields off your burst and dashes him out, so force it or wait it out — every commit is timed to it.

notes: Content-layer win[] already reads Ekko/Ekko/Skill/Ekko/Ekko/Ekko/Azir, matching the packet levelChart; only the full-layer phases[].side was stuck on 'Skill' for all seven rows, so the side edits above bring full into agreement with content — no paired win[N] edit exists to propose because the content values are already the target values. Row 2 left as Skill on both layers. packet.suspectNames flags 'Use Parallel Convergence' (wants.you[2]) and 'Save Emperor's Divide' (wants.foe[2]) — both are the correct Riot names and are FALSE POSITIVES; left untouched. Emperor's Divide terrain blocking Ekko's E dash is taken from the kit's terrain flag ('creates terrain, blocks paths and dashes'); the exact behaviour against a dash already in flight is not stated in Riot's text, so the page says it walls the E rather than claiming a specific mid-dash cancel.
